title: Tensor products of irreducible algebras over a separably closed field
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed]. Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative unital $k$-algebras, meaning commutative unital rings with fixed unital homomorphisms from $k$. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] are irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Equip $A\otimes_kB$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a\prime\otimes b\prime)=aa\prime\otimes bb\prime$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$ is irreducible. Irreducibility includes nonemptiness. No finite-generation, reducedness, or field hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible: unique-minimal-prime formulation, equivalently irreducibility of the nonempty spectra.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The final clause of [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep] says that $\Omega/k$ is purely inseparable because $k$ is separably closed. This is the characteristic-independent purely inseparable assertion; in characteristic zero the extension is trivial. Put $A_\Omega=A\otimes_k\Omega$, $B_\Omega=B\otimes_k\Omega$ and $T=(A\otimes_kB)\otimes_k\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible, first paragraph: pass to the algebraically closed purely inseparable extension; its algebraic closure can be used in place of its perfect closure.

proof.text: For each of the three commutative $k$-algebras $C=A,B,A\otimes_kB$, apply [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] to the $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and the purely inseparable extension $\Omega/k$ from Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] its base change is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_k\Omega)$, with the prescribed projection. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}A_\Omega$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B_\Omega$ are irreducible, and $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$. A homeomorphism preserves nonemptiness and the condition that two nonempty open subsets meet, hence preserves irreducibility.

source.place: Tag 00I7, first paragraph, maps induced by the purely inseparable extension (Tag 0BRA, lemma-p-ring-map); affine base-change identification Tag 01I4.

proof.text: Identify $T$ with $V=A_\Omega\otimes_\Omega B_\Omega$ as follows. Send $(a\otimes\lambda)\otimes(b\otimes\mu)$ to $(a\otimes b)\otimes\lambda\mu$; the inverse sends $(a\otimes b)\otimes\nu$ to $(a\otimes\nu)\otimes(b\otimes1)$. These formulas are balanced in each tensor variable and commute with the scalar actions. The tensor universal property and generation by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extend them to linear maps. The multiplication rule and universal property of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] show they are unital ring homomorphisms. Their composites are the identity on pure tensors: in the second composite move $\mu$ from the first factor to the second using the balancing over $\Omega$. Hence they are inverse.

source.place: Tag 00I7, first paragraph, displayed tensor base-change identification, with both maps written out.

proof.text: Write $N_C$ for the ideal of nilpotent elements of a commutative ring $C$. Apply [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] to $A_\Omega$ and $B_\Omega$, whose spectra are irreducible by Step 2: their nilradicals are proper prime ideals. Consequently $R=A_\Omega/N_{A_\Omega}$ and $S=B_\Omega/N_{B_\Omega}$ are nonzero domains. Indeed $\bar x\bar y=0$ means $xy$ lies in the corresponding prime ideal, hence $\bar x=0$ or $\bar y=0$; properness gives $1\ne0$. They remain commutative unital $\Omega$-algebras through the quotient structure maps.

source.place: Tag 00I7, second paragraph: replace the two algebras by their reductions; Tag 00ES(2), lemma-irreducible.

proof.text: Let $U=R\otimes_\Omega S$. The quotient maps induce the surjective ring homomorphism $q:V\to U$, $a\otimes b\mapsto\bar a\otimes\bar b$, by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. It is surjective since every pure tensor lifts and pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $J$ be the ideal of $V$ generated by $a\otimes1$ for $a\in N_{A_\Omega}$ and $1\otimes b$ for $b\in N_{B_\Omega}$. These generators map to zero. Conversely, $\bar a\otimes\bar b\mapsto(a\otimes b)+J$ is independent of the representatives, since changing either representative changes the result by an element of $J$. The same tensor universal property makes this a ring map $U\to V/J$, inverse to the induced map $V/J\to U$ on pure tensors. Therefore $\ker q=J$.

source.place: Tag 00I7, second paragraph, reduction of the factors; elementary tensor-quotient presentation spelling out that reduction.

proof.text: Every element of $J$ is nilpotent. Each displayed generator $a\otimes1$ or $1\otimes b$ is nilpotent by taking the same power as for $a$ or $b$. Write any $z\in J$ as a finite sum $z=\sum_{i=1}^r t_i g_i$ with such generators $g_i$, and choose $e_i\ge1$ with $g_i^{e_i}=0$. In the expansion of $z^{1+\sum_i(e_i-1)}$, every monomial contains at least $e_i$ occurrences of some $g_i$, so vanishes. For the empty sum $z=0$. Thus $\ker q=J$ consists of nilpotent elements. This uses only finitely many generators for each individual element, and does not assert that either nilradical or $J$ has a uniform nilpotence exponent.

source.place: Tag 00I7, second paragraph, justification that passing to reductions does not change the prime spectrum: explicit nil-kernel calculation.

proof.text: The nonzero $\Omega$-vector spaces $R,S$ of Step 4 have nonzero tensor product $U$ by [lem-pur-field-vector-space-tensor-nontrivial]. Suppose $U$ had a nonzero zero-divisor. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-type-limit] supplies finitely generated $\Omega$-subalgebras $R\prime\subseteq R$ and $S\prime\subseteq S$ whose tensor product has a nonzero zero-divisor. These are nonzero domains: they are unital subrings of the domains $R,S$. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed and $S\prime$ is finitely generated over $\Omega$, [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-finite-type-tensor-domain] applies with base $\Omega$, left algebra $R\prime$ and right algebra $S\prime$, and says their tensor product is a domain, a contradiction. Thus $U$ is a nonzero ring without nonzero zero-divisors, hence a domain. No finite-generation assumption on $R$ or $S$ was used.

source.place: Tag 00I7, second paragraph, finite-type reduction using Tag 00I3(2), lemma-limit-argument; final paragraph supplied by the existing algebraically closed finite-type tensor-domain theorem. The separate perfect-reduced theorem is unnecessary when zero-divisors are excluded directly.

proof.text: Since $U$ is a domain, its zero ideal is prime and its only nilpotent element is zero. Therefore the nilradical of $V$ is exactly $\ker q$: one inclusion follows by applying $q$ to a nilpotent element, and the other is Step 6. This kernel is proper since $q(1)=1\ne0$ in $U$; if $xy\in\ker q$, then $q(x)q(y)=0$, hence $q(x)=0$ or $q(y)=0$. Thus the nilradical of $V$ is prime. By [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime], $\operatorname{Spec}V$ is irreducible, including nonempty. The isomorphism $T\cong V$ of Step 3 and the homeomorphism of Step 2 give irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00I7, conclusion after the reduction; Tag 00ES(2), lemma-irreducible, for the final irreducibility criterion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible. Follows its purely inseparable scalar extension, reduction of the factors, and finite-type reduction. The existing algebraically closed finite-type tensor-domain theorem supplies the final paragraph; excluding zero-divisors directly avoids the redundant perfect-reduced intermediate theorem. Quotient maps and nil-kernel argument are expanded.
